title: Multiply Strings
summary: Given two non-negative integers as strings, return their product as a string without using any built-in BigInteger library or converting the inputs to integers directly.
statement: Given two non-negative integers as strings, return their product as a string without using any built-in BigInteger library or converting the inputs to integers directly.
constraints: 1–200 decimal digits per input. Inputs have no leading zeros except the single string '0'.
Return the product as a decimal string without leading zeros, or '0' for a zero product.
Do not convert whole input strings to integers or use a BigInteger library. Work with individual digits and carries.
hints: Use the same column multiplication used on paper; the result needs at most m+n digits.
A product of input positions i and j contributes at output positions i+j and i+j+1.
Process both inputs from right to left, add the existing lower-column value, write total%10, and carry total//10 left.
Remove only leading zero positions. Keep interior and trailing zeros, and handle a zero input explicitly.
editorial: Allocate m+n digit slots. Multiply individual digit values from right to left. For each pair, include the stored lower-column value, retain its units digit, and carry the tens contribution to the preceding slot. This ordering normalizes each lower position before it is finalized. Convert the digit list to a string after removing only leading zero slots. No whole-input numeric conversion is used. The independent offline oracle deliberately uses Python's exact whole-number multiplication instead.

tests.explanation: Two multiplied by three is six, returned as the string '6'.
The partial products are 738, 6150, and 49200; adding them gives the string '56088'.
